title: Scaling Orchestration Hub — operator controls, throughput insights, and change history
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Deliver a consolidated Fleet Orchestration UI surface that exposes operator-level scaling controls (target throughput, min/max pool sizes, pre-warm policies), a real-time and historical throughput insights dashboard, and an auditable change history with diff and rollback helpers. This work ties together autoscaling policy controls from Dedicated and the Console's observability surfaces so platform owners can safely tune throughput guarantees and respond to capacity anomalies.
background: Customers on Dedicated have asked for a single place to understand and control fleet scaling behavior. Today scaling controls are fragmented: runtime config lives in infra repos, autoscale heuristics are opaque, and audit trails are limited to raw logs. This makes it hard for capacity owners to balance cost vs SLOs or to reason about why a throughput regression occurred. Prior PM work scoped autoscale primitives (PM-27109) and runtime batching work (ENG-4128); this ticket focuses on Console UX, policy surface, and the change-history model.
objectives: 1) Surface policy knobs that map directly to runtime behaviors (target RPS / tokens-per-second, min/max GPUs, warm pool percentage, cooldown windows). 2) Provide a throughput dashboard that correlates request traffic, model variants, effective throughput, and unit costs across time. 3) Implement a human-readable, auditable change history with author, timestamp, before/after policy diff, and a one-click rollback to last known-good policy. 4) Gate dangerous actions with confirmations and (optional) two-step approvals for enterprise tenants.
acceptance_criteria: - UI exposes policy controls: target_throughput, min_replicas, max_replicas, prewarm_fraction, scale_window_seconds. - Changes are validated client-side and with backend policy checks; invalid combos rejected with actionable errors. - Throughput dashboard shows per-fleet throughput, 95/99 latency, token/sec, and cost-per-token over arbitrary date ranges. - Change history displays diffs with author & commit message; rolling back applies the previous policy and emits an audit event. - Feature flag gated behind console.feature.fleet_orchestration_v2 for gradual rollout. - Unit and e2e tests for UI flows and API contracts. - Beta release to 3 pilot accounts with rollback within 48h when patterns show throughput regressions.
engineering_notes: Backend: new /v2/fleets/{id}/scaling-policy endpoint supporting PATCH with a policy schema. Store policy versions in a versioned policy table with metadata (author, message, effective_ts). Telemetry: emit policy.change events and link them with autoscaler decisions using correlation_id. Frontend: build an interactive policy editor with validation and preview of projected capacity and cost delta. Work with ENG-4210 (autoscaler metrics stream) for real-time metrics feed. Coordinate rollout with runtime feature toggle to ensure policy keys map 1:1 to runtime flags.
rollout_plan: 1) Dark-launch UI internally for SRE + 2 pilot customers (feature flag off by default). 2) Monitor metrics for 2 weeks: mismatch rate between requested and achieved throughput, incidents triggered by policy change, cost per token delta. 3) Open beta to top 20 Dedicated customers. 4) GA with admin approval flow and organization-wide audit retention defaults. 5) Post-GA: add RBAC granularity and webhook notifications for policy changes.
metrics: Primary: percentage of policy changes that require manual rollback within 72 hours (goal <5%), median time to detect throughput regression after a policy change (goal <15m using current tracing), delta in cost-per-token after policy changes (track for regressions). Secondary: adoption rate among Dedicated accounts, mean time to apply policy (goal <30s), audit-search query latency.
qa_plan: Automated: unit tests for schema validation, API contract tests, integration test simulating autoscaler reactions to policy changes. Manual: walkthroughs with SRE team to apply policy changes, observe autoscaler behavior on staging load generator, test rollback and audit trail queries. Security: verify audit tamper-resistance and encryption of policy history in storage. Accessibility: keyboard and screen-reader checks for policy editor dialogs.
outstanding_risks: - Risk of misconfigured policies causing double-scaling or resource thrashing; mitigated by conservative defaults and canary enforcement. - Correlation between policy change and runtime decisions may be lossy if telemetry isn't propagated; dependency ENG-4210 critical. - UX complexity: exposing too many knobs could confuse non-expert users; mitigate with 'simple' and 'advanced' modes and inline guidance. - Enterprise compliance: some customers require immutable change history; need a retention and export story.
